issue.title: Refuse dirty ref-scan targets per PDF instead of failing the whole scan

task_type_fields.proposal:
Make `bob ref scan`'s dirty-target refusal per-PDF instead of scan-wide. Today
`ensure_safe_to_write` (`src/native/highlights_ref/guard.rs`) collects the write paths
of every plan, runs one `git status`, and if any touched path is dirty (and not allowed
by `dirty_entry_allowed_for_plans`) fails the whole scan with `dirty_targets` before any
PDF is written. On the Mac, Highlights autosaves annotations into `lib/**.pdf` inside the
vault, so a single PDF you are annotating that also needs a marker write can refuse the
entire 15-minute cron scan (and Bob Refs ⌘S) until vault-sync commits it.

Proposal: refuse only the PDFs whose own targets are dirty, report them per PDF (a
failure or a hold-like row in human and JSON output and the scan receipt), and let the
rest of the scan proceed. Decide whether an autosaved-but-otherwise-clean PDF should be
a hold (`retrying next scan`) rather than a failure, which would fit the hold vocabulary
added in `marker_write.rs`.

Proposed by bob-cli-at.7 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #5); filed by the bob-cli-at land agent.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
The bob-cli-at plan listed "The dirty_targets policy" under Out of scope; it is
pre-existing scan-wide behavior the coordinated-write work did not change.

issue.creation_reason: One Highlights-autosaved PDF that needs a marker write makes ensure_safe_to_write refuse every PDF in the Mac cron scan; the bob-cli-at plan left the dirty_targets policy out of scope.

payload.description: Follow-up proposed by bob-cli-at.7; builds on the coordinated marker-write executor, hold vocabulary, and decisions:open-pdf-writes-are-coordinated
